::: {.callout-note}
## What this document is

This is the first of three "intro and methods" children for the PST
freshwater effort parent document. Together with `_02_framework.qmd` and
`_03_pipeline_and_registry.qmd`, it describes the framework — scope, the Track A
tier hierarchy, the Track B derivation logic, assumptions A1–A4, design
rules R1–R5 — while the analysis children report assembly status.

This document specifically owns the deliverable contract: what was
requested, by whom, over what geography, and the scope decisions made
along the way. Framework material previously duplicated across
`PST_ANALYSIS.md` and the Background/Methods prose in
`interview_proportions.qmd` has been consolidated into these three
children; those source documents are retired.

Other children should not restate scope, tiers, or assumptions. They cite
them (e.g. "per A2") and get on with the computation.
:::

# Purpose & deliverable contract

The U.S. side of the Pacific Salmon Commission has contracted with a consultant
to update the economic valuation of PST salmon
fisheries. Commercial landings and marine recreational effort are already
accessible at the needed resolution. **Freshwater recreational effort is
not** — no standing WDFW reporting process produces angler trips broken out
by mode and location. This work fills that gap.

**Deliverable:** Year × River × Mode (guided/unguided) × Location
(bank/boat) × Angler trips, 2022–2025. **Recipient:** Melissa Errend,
Northern Economics. **Scope authority:** Jim Scott.

## Requested format

For 2022 through 2025, the consultant has requested effort data in the
following format:

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Year** | Calendar year, 2022–2025 |
| **River** | Individual river/system (rolled to block where required) |
| **Mode** | Guided vs. private (unguided) |
| **Location** | Boat vs. bank |
| **Angler trips** | Total estimated angler trips (see glossary) |

Species scope: **PST salmon, total salmon** — not species-specific.
Steelhead is excluded entirely.

## Geographic scope

| Region | In scope | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Puget Sound freshwater | Yes | Framework for annual NEPA anlysis used to estimate angler trips from CRC harvest |
| WA Coast freshwater | Yes |  |
| Columbia mainstem: middle, upper, tributaris | Yes | Delivered to the consultant directly by ODFW (OR+WA combined) |
| Columbia tributaries (WA) | Yes | |
| Columbia mainstem: Buoy 10 and Bonneville-McNary | **No** | Delivered to the consultant directly by ODFW (OR+WA combined) |
| Steelhead, any region | **No** | Out of scope by definition |


::: {.callout-note}
**Delivery scope note.** Buoy 10, Lower Columbia, and Bonneville–McNary
(the Columbia mainstem block) are **excluded from delivery**. Those ODFW
files were transmitted to WDFW *by Northern Economics* — the consultant
already has this data, so we do not send it back.
`analysis/pst/03_analysis/pst_fw_angler_trips_assembly.R` never ingests this
block; `DELIVER_BLOCKS` gates the deliverable to Puget Sound, WA Coast, and
Columbia tributaries only. The block stays in the crosswalk purely for
documentation, in case it's ever needed for internal QC.
:::

## Background & Consultant Request

The U.S. has contracted with an economics consultant to assess the economic
value of PST (Pacific Salmon Treaty) salmon fisheries. Commercial catch data
and marine recreational fishing effort data are readily accessible, but
**freshwater recreational effort** is more challenging to produce at the
resolution requested.

### Existing methods and data

**CRC-based freshwater trip estimates** already exist as part of the Puget Sound NEPA
analysis for our annual North of Falcon fishing package. The NEPA spreadsheet
(`NEPA PS_Recreational Effort Estimates 2025_2026_for 2026_2027 Projections_4_21_2026.xlsx`)
produces annual trip estimates by river and month using CRC salmon harvest
multiplied by a trips-per-salmon-caught ratio (per 2013 NOAA memo).
Two ratios were originally established: 3.44 trips/salmon in odd yeras and 8.65 trips/salmon in even years. 
Rather than use historical ratios we opted to derive trips/salmon ratios using paired creel survey and CRC harvest estimates within the data request window. In practice this extends to years/areas where CRC harvest itself isn't published yet (2025): rather than fall back to an externally published ratio, the pipeline projects that CRC harvest from its own recent history (Tier P3, `pst_crc_harvest_projection.R`) and expands it with the same self-derived ratio — no published ratio (NEPA's or otherwise) feeds any delivered number.

**Creel interview data** from WDFW's internal database contains
party-level records with guided status and bank/boat classification. These
interviews do not cover all rivers, and sample sizes vary, but they provide
the best available empirical basis for estimating the *proportional split*
by mode and location.

## Units note

The consultant's request is phrased in "angler days"; everything this
pipeline produces is angler **trips**
(`total_trips_est = total_effort_hrs / mean_trip_length`).
